title: The Bosphorus Brief — 25 September 2026
overview: A shaky earth and a shaky lira share the news cycle today. Two moderate earthquakes near Şanlıurfa closed schools but caused no major damage, while the OECD trimmed Turkey's growth outlook and flagged stubborn inflation. On the diplomatic front, Erdoğan pressed Washington on F-35 access, and a UN walkout during Netanyahu's speech drew sharply divergent coverage across outlets.

sections.heading: Earthquakes in the Southeast — Schools Closed, No Major Damage Reported
sections.body: Şanlıurfa province felt a magnitude 5.4 quake on Thursday, with a related M5.1 tremor near Hilvan also reported by EMSC and USGS. Local authorities closed schools as a precaution while damage assessments continue. There is no indication of casualties in the coverage reviewed. Residents in the region should expect aftershocks are possible and should follow provincial governor's office guidance on school and building safety; this is a normal precaution, not a sign of worsening conditions.

sections.heading: Lira and Prices: OECD Turns More Cautious
sections.body: The OECD has cut its Turkish growth forecast to the lowest since 2020 and now expects inflation to stay elevated longer, citing regional tensions including the Iran situation and rising prices. The lira sits at 48.86 to the dollar and 55.69 to the euro today. For residents budgeting in lira — rent, tuition, imported goods — this points to continued pressure rather than a sudden shift; no emergency measures have been announced.

sections.heading: F-35 Talks and the Iran Border Squeeze
sections.body: President Erdoğan said he is 'confident' Turkey will regain access to the US F-35 program, describing Trump as showing 'positive willingness' toward concrete next steps; both pro-government and international outlets covered the remarks similarly. Separately, US sanctions on Iran are creating long queues at the Turkey-Iran border, with truckers and traders uncertain whether the squeeze is easing or continuing — worth watching for anyone with cross-border business or family ties to Iran.

sections.heading: Deportation and Residency Cases to Watch
sections.body: Hana Human Rights Organization has raised concern over an imminent deportation threat facing one of its members in Turkey; details remain limited but it's a case worth following given our standing focus on foreign residents' legal security. Separately, in Germany, a Turkish national is facing deportation proceedings tied to a fatal street-racing case, an example of how criminal cases can intersect with residency status abroad. In Cyprus, one report describes a person who has gone 1,390 days without a residence permit decision — a reminder that ikamet backlogs remain a real burden for some applicants.

sections.heading: UN Speech Fallout: Divergent Framing
sections.body: Delegates walked out before Netanyahu's UN General Assembly speech, in which he called critics 'moral cowards' and accused them of antisemitism. State-aligned Al Jazeera and international outlets like the BBC covered the walkout itself fairly similarly, but independent Middle East Eye emphasized the 'near-empty hall' and Hamas's sharp rejection of the speech as 'rife with lies' — a useful reminder to read across sources on this story.

closing: Stay dry, stay steady, and check on neighbors near Şanlıurfa if you're in the area — see you tomorrow.
